cells.prior_anchor: An achievable operating point: a confinement/transport relation links field and heating to density and temperature, and a beta, density, or power limit pushes back on the choice
cells.prior_limit: P4 requires operating point jointly closed with magnets and heating over a justified, independently checked range; the selected reduced-model search retains fixed profiles, empirical transport and unqualified conductor/geometry assumptions.

cells.prior_anchor: S is not applicable: the plasma has no hardware or cost account of its own; its structure is the calc spine, and its cost lives in rows 3/4.
cells.prior_limit: No next level applies: this dimension is explicitly not applicable in the pinned rubric.

cells.prior_anchor: Replaceable units vs life-of-plant components separately sized; replacement logic follows computed life
cells.prior_limit: Component-specific design, fabrication and installation estimates with validated uncertainty remain absent; the plant-wide partial envelope does not supply them.

cells.prior_anchor: 2a: wall-load limit pushes back on the design
cells.prior_limit: P4 requires neutronics/damage closure across the build, searched and independently checked; a held calibration on a simplified torus does not provide it.

cells.prior_anchor: 2b: lifetime feeds replacement schedule and availability
cells.prior_limit: P4 requires material-specific neutronics and damage closure across the build; the shared in-vessel replacement clock does not calculate divertor erosion or shielding-dependent coil life.

cells.prior_anchor: 2c: computed TBR vs floor pushes back on blanket/build choices
cells.prior_limit: No coupled neutronics/damage design closure across the build, design search with that closure, or justified physical uncertainty model is established.

cells.prior_anchor: A stress or current-density limit pushes back on coil sizing and field choice
cells.prior_limit: P4 requires independently checked coil-set closure over a justified physical range; continuous reference-conductor sizing and local rectangular fit still lack qualified product/angle/strain data, full coil geometry and independently validated structural closure.

cells.prior_anchor: Winding pack, structure, power supplies, cryoplant costed as separately sized sub-accounts
cells.prior_limit: The limited insulation alternative does not establish design-based fabrication/installation coverage, qualified manufacturing scope and uncertainty for the complete magnet estimate.

cells.prior_anchor: Wall-plug → coupled-power chain computed with a stated deposition assumption, verified
cells.prior_limit: P3 requires both plasma-derived demand and a port, coupling or geometry limit; required demand exists, but generic efficiency-domain bounds and installed-power capacity do not establish that hardware constraint.

cells.prior_anchor: Cost follows installed heating power with source basis
cells.prior_limit: Sources, transmission and launchers need separate equipment cost accounts and replaceable-component lives.

cells.prior_anchor: A heat-flux or erosion limit pushes back on operation or geometry
cells.prior_limit: P4 needs exhaust and detachment closure, searched and independently checked; fixed reference transport/profile transfer plus an accounting identity is not that closure.

cells.prior_anchor: Cost follows divertor thermal power or area with source basis
cells.prior_limit: Targets/cassettes need explicit replaceable units with replacement logic from their own computed life.

cells.prior_anchor: Shell volume from the radial build and a computed gas-load/pumping estimate, verified
cells.prior_limit: P3 requires vessel structural or actual pumping-capacity constraints; required effective speed alone supplies neither a selected pumping train nor a capacity limit.

cells.prior_anchor: Cost follows computed shell volume/mass with source basis
cells.prior_limit: Shell, ports and pumping train need separately sized cost subaccounts.

cells.prior_anchor: The computed loop feeds the recirculation/net-power constraints so coolant choices push back on feasibility
cells.prior_limit: P4 requires thermal-hydraulic state closure across the loop; imposed temperatures, transferred fixed-layout losses and unresolved salt/conversion state remain.

cells.prior_anchor: Pumps, piping, heat exchangers as separately sized subaccounts
cells.prior_limit: S4 lacks qualified design/procurement boundaries and validation against an appropriate engineered reference; conditional partial uncertainty now exists but does not supply those missing elements.

cells.prior_anchor: Cycle responds to blanket/coolant temperature with a materials or temperature limit pushing back
cells.prior_limit: P4 requires thermodynamic state closure with the primary loop; a source-fit correlation and failed salt/steam temperature interface do not provide it.

cells.prior_anchor: Costs follow computed gross/net power with source basis
cells.prior_limit: S3 requires turbine island, electrical plant and heat sink as separately sized subaccounts; current power-rate aggregates do not provide that.

cells.prior_anchor: Buildings carry no plasma physics; their depth is structural
cells.prior_limit: No next level applies to a dimension the pinned rubric declares not applicable.

cells.prior_anchor: Building set sized by volume/function from layout drivers, incl. hot cell and remote-handling facilities
cells.prior_limit: S4 still lacks engineered/reference-validated layout and complete procurement/services boundaries; later conditional uncertainty in civil units does not cure those omissions.

cells.prior_anchor: Tritium inventory, startup requirement, and processing throughput forward-computed, verified
cells.prior_limit: Computed stock and decay affect the running breeding requirement, but calendar-dependent annual makeup remains diagnostic. Availability, physical equipment limits and obtainable startup supply do not form the integrated self-sufficiency feasibility closure required for P3.

cells.prior_anchor: Processing-plant cost follows computed throughput with source basis
cells.prior_limit: Four historical rows share an aggregate throughput law; processing subsystems are not independently sized subaccounts with appropriate lifecycle logic.

cells.prior_anchor: Availability derived from the maintenance/replacement schedule and feeds the economics, pushing back on design choices
cells.prior_limit: P4 lacks qualified maintenance sequence/logistics closure: new facilities screens use the existing calendar and preserve failed assumptions rather than close the schedule with all required outages.

cells.prior_anchor: Levelized replacement follows computed component life
cells.prior_limit: S3 requires replacement per component class plus decomposed O&M and decommissioning; new cooling classes improve replacement detail but inherited staffing/power O&M and aggregate decommissioning still fail that full conjunction.

cells.prior_anchor: The economics layer's depth is structural.
cells.prior_limit: Economics layer depth is structural; this rubric has no physics axis for R12.

cells.prior_limit: Complete bottom-up procurement coverage, engineered risk/correlation/schedule treatment and suitable reference validation are absent.
